title: FP8 calibration and task-aware metrics: implement per-profile scorers and CI gating
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Scope: Implement a standardized quality-metrics library and calibration workflow that produces per-quantization-profile scores (FP8/INT8 and hybrid variants) for both generic language-model signals (perplexity, token-LL distribution) and task-specific scorers (MMLU-style multi-subject accuracy, summarization ROUGE-L/F1, translation BLEU, classification accuracy/F1, NER F1, and custom reranker nDCG). Output artifacts must be JSONL records compatible with the existing eval-harness and Console ingestion API.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Use perplexity on held-out slices as the canonical LM-level sanity check; report both mean and median perplexity plus 95% bootstrap CI. Per-profile drift defined as >1.5x median perplexity increase vs baseline.
- Use an MMLU-style suite with stratified subject buckets (STEM, Humanities, Social Sciences) and report per-subject accuracy, macro average, and micro average. Establish gating threshold: no more than 3 percentage points absolute drop in overall MMLU accuracy compared to FP16 baseline for P0 releases.
- Task-specific metrics: summarization (ROUGE-1/2/L and BERTScore), translation (BLEU + COMET if GPU available), classification/QA (exact match + F1), retrieval/reranking (nDCG@5). All scorers run with identical tokenization and prompt templates between baseline and quantized profile.
- Calibration workflow: two-stage approach. Stage A (synthetic calibration): run calibration kernels on a small, stratified calibration set (n=2k prompts) to compute per-layer scale factors and quant clip points using KL-minimization and max-abs heuristics. Stage B (task validation): run the quantized profile against representative eval suites to compute the metrics above. Save calibration fingerprints and per-profile metadata for audit.
- Statistical checks: use bootstrap resampling (1k samples) to generate confidence intervals for each metric. Require that metric drop be statistically significant at p<0.05 before failing a gate.
- CI integration: produce a concise JSON summary for CI: {profile, baseline, delta_metrics, failed_gates}. This will be emitted to the pipeline log and to Console as a temporary artifact.

Datasets and sample sizes:
- Perplexity: Wiki-100k heldout subset (n=50k tokens sampled across lengths).
- MMLU-style: 1k per subject, 20 subjects (total 20k examples), stratified sampling.
- Summarization: CNN/DM dev sampled 500 examples.
- Translation: WMT small test sets, 1k examples.
- Classification/NA: SuperGLUE subsets as representative examples.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before marking Done):
1) Implementation of scoring library with modular scorer plugins and deterministic outputs under fixed RNG seed.
2) Calibration pipeline that emits per-profile calibration artifact and fingerprint (sha256) and a reproducible command to rebuild.
3) CI gating rule implemented in the quant-eval pipeline: compare target profile to FP16 baseline, compute bootstrap CI, and fail if statistically significant and exceeds configured deltas.
4) Dashboard ingestion: Console receives per-profile summary with metric breakdown and token-level distribution histograms.
5) Unit and integration tests covering scorers and sample-size error behavior.

Integration notes and telemetry:
- Instrument token-level likelihood distributions (histograms by position bucket) and KV cache hit interplay; expose two additional fields in output JSON: token_ll_histogram and kv_cache_hit_rate.
- Emit calibration metadata: calibration_method, dataset_id, seed, clip_values, layer_scales (serialized as comma-separated floats).
- Add per-profile tags so Console can group historic runs and enable time-series drift alerts.

QA plan and rollout:
- Stage 1 (internal): Run on dedicated cluster with 5 FP8/INT8 profiles and compare to FP16 baseline. Keep gating conservative (1.5% MMLU drop allowed for non-critical branches).
- Stage 2 (canary): Attach gating to a single non-production runtime-1.20 canary pool for a subset of models. Monitor user-facing failure rates and latency regressions for 72 hours.
- Stage 3 (general): Enable for full release once signal-stability and dashboarding confirmed.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- Should we include semantic similarity metrics (BERTScore/COMET) in the primary gate or only as advisory? Proposal: advisory for initial releases, primary for LLMs used in summarization/translation flows.
- How tightly should calibration be coupled to kernel selection? Current proposal: keep calibration artifacts independent so we can re-evaluate kernels without recalibration, but record kernel metadata.

Links to artifacts and references:
- Eval harness repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-eval/pull/189
- Calibration algorithm writeup (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/Quant+Calibration+Design
- Baseline FP16 metric snapshot: gs://redwood-evals/baselines/fp16/2025-02-01/summary.json
- Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/quant-profiles/overview

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket focuses on building a unified scorer and gating flow tied specifically to quantization profiles and per-profile calibration artifacts; it is intentionally task-aware (not just perplexity) and includes statistical resampling and CI integration for conservatism.
